question.text: A tower <math><mi>A</mi><mi>B</mi></math> leans towards west making an angle <math><mi>α</mi></math> with the vertical. The angular elevation of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>B</mi></math>, the top most point of the tower, is <math><msup><mrow><mn>6</mn><mn>0</mn></mrow><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">o</mi></mrow></msup></math> as observed from a point <math><mi>C</mi></math> due east of <math><mi>A</mi></math> at a distance of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>10</mn><mo> </mo><mi>ft</mi></math> from <math><mi>A</mi><mo>.</mo></math> If the angular elevation of <math><mi>B</mi></math> from a point <math><mi>D</mi></math> due east of <math><mi>C</mi></math> at a distance of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>20</mn><mo> </mo><mi>ft</mi></math> from <math><mi>C</mi></math> is <math><msup><mrow><mn>4</mn><mn>5</mn></mrow><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">o</mi></mrow></msup></math>, then the value of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>2</mn><mi>tan</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mi>α</mi></math> is equal to

solution.text:
By m-n theorem, we have

30cot⁡60o=10cot⁡45o-20cotπ2+α
⇒103=10+20tan⁡α
⇒2tan⁡α=3-1
